'''Yakov Matveevich Eliashberg''' (also '''Yasha Eliashberg'''; {{langx|ru|link=no|Яков Матвеевич Элиашберг}}; born 11 December 1946) is an American mathematician who was born in Leningrad, USSR. He is the Herald L. and Caroline L. Ritch Professor of Mathematics at [[Stanford University]]. His research interests are [[differential topology]], [[symplectic topology]], and [[contact topology]]. He was awarded many prizes for his work, including the [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics|Wolf Prize]] in 2020 (shared with [[Simon Donaldson]]).

== Education and career ==
[[File:Yakov_Eliashberg.jpg|thumb|Yakov Eliashberg in 1988]]
[[File:Yakov Eliashberg 2016 03.jpg|thumb|Yakov Eliashberg, Crafoord Prize Laureate in Mathematics 2016, with King [[Carl XVI Gustaf]] at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, Sweden, May 2016]]
Eliashberg received his PhD, entitled ''Surgery of Singularities of Smooth Mappings'', from [[Leningrad University]] in 1972, under the direction of [[Vladimir Rokhlin (Soviet mathematician)|Vladimir Rokhlin]].<ref name="Yakov Eliashberg at the Mathematics Genealogy Project">{{MathGenealogy |id=39146 }}</ref>

Due to the growing [[Antisemitism in the Soviet Union|anti-Semitism in the Soviet Union]], from 1972 to 1979 he had to work at the [[Syktyvkar State University]] in the isolated [[Komi Republic]]. In 1980 Eliashberg returned to Leningrad and applied for a visa, but his request was denied and he became a [[refusenik]] until 1987. He was cut off from mathematical life and was prevented to work in academia, but due to a friend's intercession, he managed to secure a job in industry as the head of a computer software group.<ref name="Wolf Foundation-2020">{{Cite web |date=2020-01-13 |title=Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://wolffund.org.il/2020/01/13/yakov-eliashberg/ |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US |archive-date=2020-01-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200113110714/https://wolffund.org.il/2020/01/13/yakov-eliashberg/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Schulman |first1=Julia |last2=Hsieh |first2=Michael |date=2021-02-11 |title=Coffin Problems: Soviet Anti-Semitism Buried Rising Jewish Scientists |url=https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/science/articles/coffin-problems-soviet-anti-semitism-scientists |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=Tablet Magazine}}</ref><ref name="American Mathematical Society-2009">{{Cite book |url=https://www.ams.org/books/crmp/049/crmp049-endmatter.pdf |title=New perspectives and challenges in symplectic field theory |date=2009 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |others=Miguel Abreu, François Lalonde, Leonid Polterovich |isbn=978-0-8218-4356-7 |location=Providence, R.I. |oclc=370387862}}</ref>

In 1988 Eliashberg managed to move to the United States, and since 1989 he has been Herald L. and Caroline L. Ritch professor of mathematics at [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |title=Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://mathematics.stanford.edu/people/yakov-eliashberg |access-date=2022-08-09 |website=mathematics.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref> Between 2001 and 2002 he was Distinguished Visiting professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-12-09 |title=Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/yakov-eliashberg |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref>

{{as of|2026}}, he supervised 43 PhD students, including [[Eric Katz]], [[Emmy Murphy]] and [[John Pardon]].<ref name="Yakov Eliashberg at the Mathematics Genealogy Project" />

== Research ==
Eliashberg's research interests are in [[differential topology]], especially in [[Symplectic topology|symplectic]] and [[contact topology]].<ref name="American Mathematical Society-2009" />

In the 80's he developed a combinatorial technique<ref name="Eliashberg, Ya M.-1986" /> which he used to prove that the group of [[symplectomorphism]]s is <math>\mathcal{C}^0</math>-[[Closed subset|closed]] in the [[diffeomorphism group]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Eliashberg |first=Ya. M. |date=1987-07-01 |title=A theorem on the structure of wave fronts and its applications in symplectic topology |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02577138 |journal=Functional Analysis and Its Applications |language=en |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=227–232 |doi=10.1007/BF02577138 |s2cid=121961311 |issn=1573-8485|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This fundamental result, proved also in a different way by [[Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)|Gromov]],<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-02267-2 |title=Partial Differential Relations |year=1986 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-662-02267-2|last1=Gromov |first1=Mikhael |isbn=978-3-642-05720-5 }}</ref> is now called the Eliashberg–Gromov theorem, and is one of the first manifestations of symplectic rigidity.

In 1990 he discovered a complete topological characterization of [[Stein manifold]]s of [[complex dimension]] greater than 2.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Eliashberg |first=Yakov |date=1990-03-01 |title=Topological characterization of stein manifolds of dimension >2 |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0129167X90000034 |journal=International Journal of Mathematics |volume=01 |issue=1 |pages=29–46 |doi=10.1142/S0129167X90000034 |issn=0129-167X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Eliashberg classified [[contact structure]]s into "tight" and "overtwisted" ones.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Eliashberg |first=Y. |date=1989-10-01 |title=Classification of overtwisted contact structures on 3-manifolds |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01393840 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=98 |issue=3 |pages=623–637 |doi=10.1007/BF01393840 |bibcode=1989InMat..98..623E |s2cid=121666486 |issn=1432-1297|arxiv=1404.6157 }}</ref> Using this dichotomy, he gave the complete classification of contact structures on the [[3-sphere]].<ref name="Eliashberg-1992" /> Together with [[William Thurston|Thurston]], he developed the theory of confoliations, which unifies [[foliation]]s and contact structures.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Eliashberg |first1=Y. |title=Confoliations |last2=Thurston |first2=William P. |date=1998 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |isbn=0-8218-0776-5 |location=Providence, R.I. |oclc=37748408 |author-link2=William Thurston}}</ref>

Eliashberg worked on various aspects of the [[Homotopy principle|h-principle]], introduced by [[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhail Gromov]], and he wrote in 2002 an introductory book on the subject.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Eliashberg |first1=Y. |title=Introduction to the h-principle |last2=Mishachev |first2=N. |date=2002 |isbn=0-8218-3227-1 |location=Providence, Rhode Island |oclc=49312496}}</ref>

Together with [[Alexander Givental|A. Givental]] and [[Helmut Hofer|H. H. W. Hofer]], Eliashberg pioneered the foundations of [[Floer homology#Symplectic field theory (SFT)|symplectic field theory]].<ref>{{Citation |last1=Eliashberg |first1=Y. |chapter=Introduction to Symplectic Field Theory |date=2010 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-0346-0425-3_4 |title=Visions in Mathematics: GAFA 2000 Special volume, Part II |pages=560–673 |editor-last=Alon |editor-first=N. |place=Basel |publisher=Birkhäuser |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-0346-0425-3_4 |isbn=978-3-0346-0425-3 |access-date=2022-08-09 |last2=Glvental |first2=A. |last3=Hofer |first3=H. |s2cid=6725644 |author-link2=Alexander Givental |author-link3=Helmut Hofer |editor2-last=Bourgain |editor2-first=J. |editor2-link=Jean Bourgain |editor3-last=Connes |editor3-first=A. |editor-link3=Alain Connes |editor4-last=Gromov |editor4-first=M.|editor4-link=Misha Gromov|arxiv=math/0010059 }}</ref>

==Awards==
Eliashberg received the "Young Mathematician" Prize from the [[Leningrad Mathematical Society]] in 1972.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SPb. Math. Society: the awards |url=http://www.mathsoc.spb.ru/mol_mat.html |access-date=2022-08-09 |website=[[Saint Petersburg Mathematical Society]]}}</ref> He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1986,<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 1986 |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |year=1986 |editor-last=Gleason |editor-first=Andrew M. |editor-link=Andrew M. Gleason |volume=1 |location=Berkeley |pages=531–539}}</ref> 1998<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1998.2/ICM1998.2.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 1998 |publisher=[[German Mathematical Society]] |year=1998 |editor-last=Louis |editor-first=Alfred K. |volume=2 |location=Berlin |pages=327–338 |editor-last2=Schneider |editor-first2=Peter |editor-link2=Peter Schneider (mathematician)}}</ref> and 2006 (plenary lecture).<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM2006.2/ICM2006.2.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 2006 |publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]] |year=2007 |editor-last=Sanz-Solé |editor-first=Marta |editor-link=Marta Sanz-Solé |volume=1 |location=Madrid |pages=217–246 |editor-last2=Soria |editor-first2=Javier |editor-last3=Varona |editor-first3=Juan Luis |editor-last4=Verdera |editor-first4=Joan}}</ref> In [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1995|1995]] he was a recipient of the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/yakov-eliashberg/ |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |language=en-US |archive-date=2022-08-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220808211516/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/yakov-eliashberg/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2001 Eliashberg was awarded the [[Oswald Veblen Prize in Geometry]] from the [[american mathematical society|AMS]] for his work in [[symplectic topology|symplectic]] and [[contact topology]],<ref>{{Cite journal |title=2001 Veblen Prize |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200104/comm-veblen.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the AMS]] |volume=48 |issue=4 |pages=408–410}}</ref> in particular for his proof of the [[symplectic rigidity]]<ref name="Eliashberg, Ya M.-1986">{{cite book |author=Eliashberg, Ya M. |title=Proc. of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1986 |year=1986 |pages=531–539 |chapter=Combinatorial methods in symplectic geometry}}</ref> and the development of 3-dimensional [[contact topology]].<ref name="Eliashberg-1992">{{Cite journal |last=Eliashberg |first=Yakov |date=1992 |title=Contact 3-manifolds twenty years since J. Martinet's work |url=https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/AIF_1992__42_1-2_165_0/ |journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier |volume=42 |issue=1–2 |pages=165–192 |doi=10.5802/aif.1288 |issn=0373-0956|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 2002 Eliashberg was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the US<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/yakov-eliashberg-opeuws/ |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> and in 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2012-12-02.</ref> He also was a member of the Selection Committee in mathematical sciences of the [[Shaw Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Award Presentation Ceremony 2012 {{!}} The Shaw Prize |url=http://www.shawprize.org/events/award-presentation-ceremony-2012 |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=www.shawprize.org |language=en}}</ref> He received a [[Doctorat Honoris Causa]] from the [[ENS Lyon]] in 2009<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mangin |first=Fabienne |date=2019 |title=La remise des insignes de Docteur 'Honoris Causa', une tradition au sein de l'ENS de Lyon |trans-title=The presentation of the insignia of doctor "Honoris Causa", a tradition within the ENS of Lyon |url=https://alumni.ens-lyon.fr/article/la-remise-des-insignes-de-docteur-honoris-causa-une-tradition-au-sein-de-l-ens-de-lyon/14/11/2019/76 |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=alumni.ens-lyon.fr |language=fr}}</ref> and from the [[University of Uppsala]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Piehl |first=Jakob |title=Honorary Doctors of the Faculty of Science and Technology - Uppsala University, Sweden |url=https://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/science-and-technology/ |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=www.uu.se |language=en}}</ref>

In 2013 Eliashberg shared with [[Helmut Hofer]] the [[Heinz Hopf Prize]] from the [[ETH]], Zurich, for their pioneering research in symplectic topology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Laureates 2013 |url=https://math.ethz.ch/news-and-events/events/lecture-series/heinz-hopf-prize-and-lectures/laureates/lauteates-2013.html |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=math.ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref> In 2016 Yakov Eliashberg was awarded the [[Crafoord Prize]] in Mathematics from the [[Swedish Academy of Sciences]] ''for the development of contact and symplectic topology and groundbreaking discoveries of rigidity and flexibility phenomena.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Crafoord Prizes in Mathematics and Astronomy 2016 |url=https://www.crafoordprize.se/press_release/the-crafoord-prizes-in-mathematics-and-astronomy-2016}}</ref>

In 2020 he received the [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics]] (jointly with [[Simon K. Donaldson]]).<ref name="Wolf Foundation-2020" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Stanford |date=2020-01-17 |title=Yakov Eliashberg awarded Wolf Prize in Mathematics |url=https://news.stanford.edu/2020/01/17/yakov-eliashberg-awarded-wolf-prize-mathematics/ |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=Stanford News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kehoe |first=Elaine |date=2020-06-01 |title=Donaldson and Eliashberg Awarded 2020 Wolf Prize |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=67 |issue=6 |pages=1 |doi=10.1090/noti2109 |s2cid=225820459 |issn=0002-9920|doi-access=free }}</ref> He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/yakov-eliashberg |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref> For 2023 he was awarded the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in Basic Sciences (jointly with [[Claire Voisin]]).<ref>[https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/ BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award 2023]</ref>
